\section{One exact conditional marginalization}\label{sec:marginal}

Use the decomposition $A=My+Nz$ from \eqref{eq:decomposition}.  Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cylinder}
 \cY_r=\{y\in\R^{51}:\norm y\le r/20\},\qquad
 \cD_r=\{z\in\R^{357}:\norm z\le r/2\}.
\end{equation}
Since $\norm M\le5$,
\[
 \norm{My+Nz}\le5(r/20)+r/2=3r/4.
\]
The product cylinder therefore lies strictly inside $\cC_r$.

For $y\in\cY_r$, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conditional-law}
 Z_t(y)=\int_{\cD_r}e^{-S_t(My+Nz)}\dd z,\qquad
 \nu_{t,y}(\dd z)=Z_t(y)^{-1}e^{-S_t(My+Nz)}\mathbf1_{\cD_r}(z)\dd z
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-action}
 S_t^{\eff}(y)=-\log Z_t(y).
\end{equation}
These are the exactly normalized conditional law and effective action of the
reduced heat-kernel density restricted to the declared cylinder.

\begin{theorem}[Verified finite-block marginalization]\label{thm:main}
On the side-two four-dimensional cubical block with rooted lexicographic tree
gauge, retained map \eqref{eq:selected-rows}, radius $r=10^{-5}$, and
$0<t\le10^{-18}$, the following assertions hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The scalar reduced, retained, and fiber dimensions are $136$, $17$, and
$119$; their $\suTwo$ dimensions are $408$, $51$, and $357$.
\item Tree gauge gives the exact Haar factorization
\eqref{eq:haar-factorization}.  The cotree curvature form satisfies
$H\ge\frac1{25}\Id$.
\item The exact nonlinear action \eqref{eq:exact-action} satisfies
\eqref{eq:eta-bound}--\eqref{eq:tau-bound}; the curvature chart is
$199/1000$ lower Lipschitz.
\item For every $y\in\cY_r$, the conditional potential on $\cD_r$ is strongly
convex:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fiber-convexity}
 tD_z^2S_t(My+Nz)\succeq\frac3{80}\Id.
\end{equation}
The normalized conditional laws obey
\begin{equation}\label{eq:transport-bound}
 W_2(\nu_{t,y},\nu_{t,y'})\le\frac13\norm{y-y'}
 \qquad(y,y'\in\cY_r).
\end{equation}
\item The local effective action is $C^2$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-hessian-bound}
 \norm{tD^2S_t^{\eff}(y)-\Id_{51}}\le\frac1{15}.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:effective-coercivity}
 \frac{14}{15}\Id_{51}\preceq tD^2S_t^{\eff}(y)
 \preceq\frac{16}{15}\Id_{51}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
All conclusions are uniform over the displayed cylinder and time interval.
They do not concern the unrestricted interacting density outside that
cylinder.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first three items collect Propositions~\ref{prop:dimensions},
\ref{prop:action-norm}, Theorem~\ref{thm:cotree-coercivity}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:injectivity}.  For the last two, write
\[
 tS_t(My+Nz)=\tfrac12\norm y^2
 +\tfrac12 z^{\mathsf T}H_Fz+W_t(y,z),
 \qquad H_F=N^{\mathsf T}HN.
\]
By $H_F\ge1/25$ and \eqref{eq:eta-bound},
\[
 \norm{D_z^2W_t}<\frac1{400},\qquad
 \norm{D_zD_yW_t}<\frac5{400}=\frac1{80},\qquad
 \norm{D_y^2W_t}<\frac{25}{400}=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus $D_z^2(tS_t)\succeq1/25-1/400=3/80$, proving
\eqref{eq:fiber-convexity}.  Strong log-concavity on the common convex domain,
the logarithmic Sobolev inequality, and its transport consequence
\cite{OttoVillani2000} give
\[
 W_2(\nu_{t,y},\nu_{t,y'})
 \le\frac{1/80}{3/80}\norm{y-y'}=\frac13\norm{y-y'}.
\]

Compactness of $\cD_r$ justifies differentiation under the integral.  The
exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hessian-identity}
 D^2S_t^{\eff}
 =\E_{\nu_{t,y}}[D_y^2S_t]
  -\Cov_{\nu_{t,y}}(D_yS_t,D_yS_t)
\end{equation}
and the Brascamp--Lieb covariance inequality
\cite{BrascampLieb1976} imply
\[
 \norm{tD^2S_t^{\eff}-\Id}
 \le\frac1{16}+\frac{(1/80)^2}{3/80}
 =\frac1{15}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:effective-hessian-bound} and
\eqref{eq:effective-coercivity}.  Appendix~\ref{app:marginal} gives the
regularization argument for the hard convex boundary.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Declared reference complement]\label{prop:reference-tail}
Let $\gamma_{t,F}$ be the unrestricted centered tangent Gaussian on
$\R^{357}$ with precision $H_F/t$.  Then, for $0<t\le10^{-18}$,
\[
 \gamma_{t,F}(\norm z>r/2)\le\frac{357}{10^6}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:cotree-coercivity} gives
$\E\norm Z^2=t\operatorname{tr}H_F^{-1}\le357\cdot25t$.
Markov's inequality at $r/2=1/200000$ gives the result.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Proposition~\ref{prop:reference-tail} is a calibration of the tangent
reference only.  Nonlinear action control inside a chart cannot by itself
bound the normalization or probability of the complement under the full
interacting link measure.  That missing estimate is the first open bridge to
an iterated construction.
\end{remark}
